'''Brian M. Hoffman''' (born August 7, 1941, in [[Chicago]]) is an American bioinorganic and physical chemist.

==Career==
Hoffman is a graduate of [[Lane Tech High School]] in Chicago. He studied chemistry at the [[University of Chicago]] receiving a bachelor's degree in 1962 and at [[Caltech]] with a PhD in chemistry in 1966 under the direction of [[Harden M. McConnell]]. Hoffman was briefly a postdoctoral scholar with [[Alexander Rich]] at [[MIT]]. In 1967 he started his appointment at [[Northwestern University]], where he has remained throughout his career.

Hoffman was elected to the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hoffman |first=Brian M. |title=Brian M. Hoffman |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/brian-m-hoffman-ezpwaf/ |website=[[The National Academy of Sciences]] |access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref> In 2022, he won the [[American Institute of Chemists]]'s [[American Institute of Chemists Gold Medal|Gold Medal]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Gold Medal Award Winners (2020 - 2029) |url=https://www.theaic.org/award_winners/goldmedal.html#gma20s |website=[[American Institute of Chemists]] |access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref>{{primary source inline|date=October 2025}}

==Research==
In early work, Hoffman demonstrated the reconstitution of myoglobin with cobalt in place of iron.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hoffman |first1=B. M. |last2=Petering |first2=D. H. |title=Coboglobins: Oxygen-Carrying Cobalt-Reconstituted Hemoglobin and Myoglobin |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=1970 |volume=67 |issue=2 |pages=637–643 |doi=10.1073/pnas.67.2.637 |doi-access=free |pmid=4331717 |pmc=283253 |bibcode=1970PNAS...67..637H }}</ref> Over the course of his research career, he also contributed to the study of [[cytochrome P450]], [[nitric oxide synthase]], nickel-iron [[hydrogenase]], and [[nitrogenase]].<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Hoffman BM, Lukoyanov D, Dean DR, Seefeldt LC |year=2013 |title=Nitrogenase: A Draft Mechanism |journal=Accounts of Chemical Research |volume=46 |pages=587–595|issue=2 |doi=10.1021/ar300267m|pmc=3578145 |pmid=23289741}}</ref>

Hoffman contributed to the use of electron-nuclear double-resonance ([[ENDOR]]) spectroscopy, usually to study [[enzyme mechanism]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Hoffman BM |year=2003 |title=ENDOR of Metalloenzymes |journal=Accounts of Chemical Research |volume=36 |pages=522–529|issue=7 |doi=10.1021/ar0202565|pmid=12859213 }}</ref>

He has demonstrated that [[radical SAM enzymes]], which are pervasive, operate via the transient formation of an Fe-carbon bond.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Hoffman BM, Broderick WE, Broderick JB | title = Mechanism of Radical Initiation in the Radical SAM Enzyme Superfamily | journal = Annual Review of Biochemistry | volume = 92 | issue = 1 | pages = 333–349 | date = June 2023 | pmid = 37018846 | doi = 10.1146/annurev-biochem-052621-090638 | s2cid = 257983715 | doi-access = free | pmc = 10759928 }}</ref>
